title: An instance dropped from the Library follows its original
goal: Once something is a component, you should be able to drop copies of it and have them stay connected. Dragging a component out of the Library places a linked copy. Editing the original updates every copy at once, including copies inside other things, and the app says how many it changed.
notes:
Step C5 of docs/design/ui-building.md, after make-component. Decision card to open when claimed: does a dropped instance start from the original configuration or the last one that person used (components.html leaves this open). The insert gestures come from components.html: drag, double-click, duplicate, and later the agent.

Objective: ui-components (staged now, under the focus). Create once, reuse everywhere is half of the sub epic title, and this is that half.
acceptance: Dragging a component tile onto the canvas places a linked instance, marked as an instance on the canvas and in the layers list
Double-clicking a tile inserts one at the center, and duplicating an instance keeps it linked
Editing the original updates every instance in one undo step, with a brief confirmation naming how many changed
An instance nested inside another component also updates
Core logic is covered by tests in PhotonzCore written before the implementation
Audit written under queue/audits/, anything rough filed as a follow-up

log.note: Adversarial review before building. (1) The decision the task asks for is not a decision yet: 'does a copy start from the original or from the last one you configured' presupposes overrides, and there are none until C6, so there is nothing a person could see either way. Recorded rather than filed as a card. (2) The real hazard is descending: the canvas already goes one level in on a double click, so a copy you could open would let you edit a piece that the next edit of the original silently overwrites. A copy is therefore ONE object: clicks pick it whole, double click does not enter it, its layers row has no twist open, and nothing can be dropped inside it. Overrides are the supported way in, and they are C6. (3) A copy must read as a copy: the original keeps the filled violet mark and its name, a copy wears the same mark outlined and no name, because a name over each of twelve buttons is twelve labels. (4) Deleting the original must not delete the copies: they stay exactly as they look, as ordinary groups. (5) Double click on a component tile currently selects the original, which collides with insert. Insert wins, because that is already what double click does on a Media tile; Select on Canvas stays the button it already is. (6) A dropped copy joins the frame it lands on, the same rule a drawn shape follows, or dropping a button on a phone screen leaves it floating off the screen. (7) Cut as decorative for this step: exposed properties, variant pickers, an override list, a swap-component menu. Kept: a copies count on the shelf tile, because 'how many of these are out there' is the question the shelf raises.

Copies that follow their original shipped in Next behind next-components (commit fcdb672). Dragging a Library tile onto the canvas, double clicking it, or Layer > Insert Component all place a copy centred on the drop and joined to the frame under it; Command J keeps a copy linked; editing the original updates every copy in one undo step with a pill saying how many followed. A copy is one object (click picks it whole, no descending, no twist open, no drops inside), marked by one violet diamond against the original's four. Model is PhotonzCore/ComponentInstances.swift with the sync inside History.perform; 26 new tests in ComponentInstanceTests, whole suite green at 1764. Verified in the probe app with Scripts/playtest/component-instance-walk.json, real window captures. Audit: queue/audits/2026-09-03-component-instances.json. Follow-up filed: a-copy-follows-the-original-when-its-look-change.
